narrative:
Your loan application was carefully reviewed by our machine learning model, which analyzes patterns from past credit decisions in 1970s Germany to predict risks. Based on your details—like requesting 4795 Deutsche Marks for a radio or TV over 36 months, with a checking account balance under 200 DM, savings below 100 DM, less than a year at your current job and residence, no property assets listed, and owning your housing—the model estimated a 63% probability that you might face challenges repaying, classifying you as a bad credit risk and leading to denial.

The three key factors that most strongly influenced this decision were your checking account status, property situation, and the loan duration. Your checking account with no more than 200 DM stood out as a major concern, as it pushed the prediction toward higher risk—unlike many approved applicants, where half had no checking account at all and only about a quarter were in your range. Similarly, having no known property or assets like a car, real estate, or savings plans was a significant red flag, since just 12% of those approved shared this situation, while most had something tangible.

Your requested loan duration of 36 months also contributed notably to the risk assessment, being nearly double the average 19 months for approved applicants, suggesting stretched finances over time. While positives like your existing paid credit history, no other installment plans or debtors, and a management or skilled job helped pull toward approval, they weren't enough to offset these top concerns. Compared to typical approved applicants—who often had steadier employment over years, lower amounts around 2900 DM, and assets to back repayment—your profile appeared riskier in these core areas.

To improve your chances next time, consider building up your checking or savings balance, shortening the loan term, or acquiring verifiable assets like property. You might also provide more details on employment stability or reduce the amount requested to align closer with approved profiles. Reapplying after strengthening these areas could make a real difference.
